[
  {
    "n": 1,
    "title": "Definition and Rigorous Foundation of Separable Equations",
    "scope": "Establishes the standard definition of first-order separable differential equations in derivative and symmetrical differential forms. Proves why separation works from scratch using antiderivatives and the chain rule of differentiation. Delineates the boundary between general first-order forms dy/dx = f(x, y) and strictly separable structures.",
    "key_points": [
      "Standard first-order ODE form: dy/dx = f(x, y)",
      "Separable differential form: f1(y) dy = f2(x) dx or M(y) dy + N(x) dx = 0 with continuous coefficient functions",
      "Antiderivatives H1'(y) = M(y) and H2'(x) = N(x)",
      "Chain rule justification: (d/dy)H1(y) * (dy/dx) = (d/dx)H1(y), yielding d/dx [H1(y) + H2(x)] = 0",
      "Implicit solution representation: H1(y) + H2(x) = C for an arbitrary constant C"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 2,
    "title": "Solution Representations, Curve Families, and Initial Value Problems",
    "scope": "Distinguishes between implicit and explicit general solutions as well as general versus particular integrals. Introduces the geometric concept of a family of integral curves and the selection of a single trajectory through initial conditions. Discusses the analytic boundaries of explicit expression and the motivation for numerical approximation.",
    "key_points": [
      "Differentiable function y = phi(x) satisfying an implicit relation Phi(x, y) = 0",
      "General solution and general integral representing an infinite family of solution curves",
      "Initial value problem (IVP): f1(y) dy = f2(x) dx subject to y(x0) = y0",
      "Definite integral formulation: integral from y0 to y of f1(u) du = integral from x0 to x of f2(v) dv",
      "Particular solution / particular integral selecting a single unique curve",
      "Analytical intractability of explicit inversion y(x) and role of numerical methods"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 3,
    "title": "Separation Algorithm and Singularities: Lost and Extraneous Solutions",
    "scope": "Details the systematic two-step algebraic method for separating variables via ratios and integrating both sides. Analyzes critical domain hazards encountered during algebraic division, specifically the loss of singular solutions and generation of spurious branches. Formulates a verification protocol for roots of divisor functions.",
    "key_points": [
      "Canonical form: f1(x) g1(y) dx = f2(x) g2(y) dy",
      "Two-step algorithm: isolate variable groups via proportions [f1(x)/f2(x)] dx = [g2(y)/g1(y)] dy, then integrate both sides",
      "Loss of particular/singular solutions when dividing by terms that vanish: f2(x) g1(y) = 0",
      "Appearance of extraneous solutions when functions exhibit discontinuities where 1 / [f2(x) g1(y)] = 0",
      "Mandatory verification step checking if roots of g1(y) = 0 or f2(x) = 0 satisfy the original differential equation"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 4,
    "title": "Geometric Separable Modeling: Circular Integral Trajectories",
    "scope": "Examines the archetype separable problem dy/dx = -x/y and its complete algebraic resolution. Connects the algebraic solution to geometric orthogonal trajectories and families of curves in the Cartesian plane. Demonstrates how setting a specific constant isolates an individual circular curve from concentric orbits.",
    "key_points": [
      "Differential equation: dy/dx = -x/y",
      "Separation of differentials: x dx = -y dy",
      "Integration: integral x dx = - integral y dy + C yielding x^2 + y^2 = C^2",
      "Geometric realization: concentric circle family centered at the origin",
      "Evaluation of a specific trajectory (e.g., C^2 = 5 with radius sqrt(5))"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 5,
    "title": "Algebraic Case Study: Partial Fractions, Domain Division, and Singular Recovery",
    "scope": "Provides a rigorous worked study of xy' + y = y^2 with initial condition y(1) = 0.5. Emphasizes partial fraction decomposition during integration and meticulous accounting of domain restrictions. Illustrates how divided constants absorb signs and how singular solutions relate to parameter limits.",
    "key_points": [
      "Equation reorganization: x (dy/dx) = y^2 - y",
      "Separation: dy / (y^2 - y) = dx / x under constraints x != 0, y != 0, y != 1",
      "Partial fraction integration: integral [1/(y - 1) - 1/y] dy = integral dx / x + C",
      "Logarithmic resolution: ln|(y - 1) / y| = ln|c x|, leading to (y - 1)/y = c x",
      "General solution formulation: y = 1 / (1 - c x) or y = 1 + c x y, alongside singular solution y = 0",
      "Identification that y = 1 corresponds to c = 0, while y = 0 is lost during division",
      "Particular solution computation: y(1) = 0.5 yields c = -1, producing y = 1 / (1 + x)"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 6,
    "title": "Linear Population Dynamics: The Malthusian Model",
    "scope": "Formulates the classical Malthusian model of unrestricted exponential growth and decay from first principles. Solves the resulting separable initial value problem and interprets parameter signs. Evaluates historical demographic forecasting, sensitivities to net growth rates, and structural failure modes.",
    "key_points": [
      "Derivation from net rate r = alpha - beta: dN/dt = (alpha - beta) N with N(0) = N0",
      "Separation and integration: dN / N = (alpha - beta) dt yielding ln N = (alpha - beta) t + C",
      "Closed-form particular solution: N(t) = N0 * exp((alpha - beta) t)",
      "Regime classification: exponential explosion (alpha > beta), extinction (alpha < beta), and static equilibrium (alpha = beta)",
      "Parametric growth comparisons across historical growth constants r and long-term unphysical divergences"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 7,
    "title": "Nonlinear Population Dynamics: Verhulst Logistic Model and Saturation",
    "scope": "Develops the Verhulst logistic growth model incorporating environmental carrying capacity. Solves the nonlinear ODE using partial fraction expansion and isolates the explicit population trajectory over time. Analyzes asymptotic behavior across initial population regimes and surveys real biological applications.",
    "key_points": [
      "Model formulation: dN/dt = alpha * (1 - N / Np) * N with carrying capacity Np and alpha > 0",
      "Separation of variables: Np dN / [(Np - N) N] = alpha dt",
      "Partial fraction decomposition: [1/N + 1/(Np - N)] dN = alpha dt",
      "Integration and constant determination: ln[N / (Np - N)] = alpha t + ln[N0 / (Np - N0)]",
      "Closed-form logistic solution: N(t) = [Np N0 exp(alpha t)] / [Np + N0 (exp(alpha t) - 1)]",
      "Qualitative asymptotic regimes: S-shaped logistic inflection for N0 < Np, constant equilibrium for N0 = Np, and decay toward Np for N0 > Np",
      "Empirical applications: Rhizopertha dominica grain beetle populations, historical census ceilings, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacterial cultures"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 8,
    "title": "Reduction to Separable Form I: Linear Arguments y' = f(ax + by)",
    "scope": "Presents substitution theory for first-order ODEs whose right-hand side depends entirely on a linear combination of independent and dependent variables. Derives the transformed separable equation for the new dependent variable. Demonstrates execution via a concrete worked example.",
    "key_points": [
      "Target structure: dy/dx = f(ax + by)",
      "Substitution definition: z = ax + by with differential relation dz/dx = a + b(dy/dx)",
      "Separable transformed ODE: dz/dx = a + b f(z)",
      "General quadrature formula: x = integral [dz / (a + b f(z))] + C",
      "Worked example dy/dx = 1/(x - y) + 1: substitution z = x - y produces dz/dx = -1/z",
      "Integration yielding z^2 / 2 = -x + C and final implicit solution (x - y)^2 = -2x + c"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 9,
    "title": "Reduction to Separable Form II: Homogeneous Equations y' = f(y/x)",
    "scope": "Defines homogeneous first-order differential equations characterized by scale-invariant arguments y/x. Establishes the substitution z = y/x using the product rule and derives the separated integral format. Solves a trigonometric homogeneous differential equation to completion.",
    "key_points": [
      "Definition: dy/dx = f(y/x)",
      "Substitution z = y/x leading to y = z x and derivative dy/dx = z + x(dz/dx)",
      "Separated ODE: x(dz/dx) = f(z) - z yielding dz / [f(z) - z] = dx / x",
      "General integral formula: x = C * exp(integral [dz / (f(z) - z)])",
      "Worked example dy/dx = y/x + tan(y/x): reduction to x(dz/dx) = tan(z)",
      "Integration: integral (cos z / sin z) dz = integral dx / x + C giving ln|sin z| = ln|x| + ln c",
      "Final explicit relation: sin(y/x) = c x"
    ]
  },
  {
    "n": 10,
    "title": "Reduction to Separable Form III: Linear Fractional Arguments",
    "scope": "Addresses differential equations with arguments composed of ratios of linear polynomials. Classifies the system into intersecting and parallel cases based on coefficient determinants. Details the geometric translation of coordinates to eliminate constant offsets and the alternative linear substitution for parallel systems.",
    "key_points": [
      "General form: dy/dx = f((a1 x + b1 y + c1) / (a2 x + b2 y + c2))",
      "System classification via line intersection: a1 x + b1 y + c1 = 0 and a2 x + b2 y + c2 = 0",
      "Case 1 (Intersecting lines, a1 b2 - a2 b1 != 0): coordinate translation to intersection point (x*, y*) via X = x - x*, Y = y - y*",
      "Invariance of derivatives dY/dX = dy/dx leading to homogeneous equation dY/dX = phi(Y/X)",
      "Case 2 (Parallel lines, a1 b2 - a2 b1 = 0): proportional coefficients a2 x + b2 y = k(a1 x + b1 y)",
      "Reduction of parallel case to dy/dx = F(a1 x + b1 y), solvable via substitution z = a1 x + b1 y"
    ]
  }
]
